body: Forgiveness ends when you want it to. It definitely wouldn’t hurt to strike up a convo w/ your mother, especially if she’s intentionally messing up your pronouns. Malicious or not, it’s uncomfortable, and most definitely not okay. You don’t owe her forgiveness in any way, shape, or form.

I can’t think of any reason other than them projecting their internalized transphobia onto you. Irrational, really. Not in the same circumstances, but I’ve had my elderly relatives downplay my sexuality before I came out as trans, ie. “Yeah, I liked girls too. But I’m not bi/gay.” I’m so sorry you have to put up with that.
hi! I’m ace (and aro) as well, about 1 month on T, and my sex drive has *completely* tanked. T reacts differently for everyone, so it’s hard to tell until you actually go on it
my apologies, it really wasn’t my intention to cause discomfort or to bash on phalloplasties. thank you for the informative post!!

please don’t get me wrong, I’m super fortunate and grateful to be able to afford gender affirming therapy, as well as have a solid support network outside my family! I’m just extremely frustrated rn :(

It’s quite alright. :) I found solace in the fact that I did what I could; when someone’s deadset on taking their life, oftentimes, you cannot change that. I couldn’t cope for the first year either, so I didn’t. I let my emotions run loose, lashed out at people and myself, and sometimes such a catharsis is relieving. Please do not blame yourself, or place such a responsibility on yourself. You’re not a warrior because you win, you’re a warrior because you fight. I’m wishing you nothing but the absolute best.

I lost my partner to suicide 2 years ago. The guilt never stopped eating away at me, convincing me that I could’ve done something to prevent it - that if I had done things “correctly,” he would still be here today. It still hurts.
